rationale: The Court is most likely to produce a Roberts opinion rejecting categorical or presumptive presidential criminal immunity while endorsing a narrow, act-by-act framework with heightened safeguards (official-act line-drawing and privilege/evidentiary limits) for core Article II functions. Multiple separate writings are likely: dissents emphasizing chilling/retaliation concerns (Thomas/Alito/Kavanaugh) and concurrences refining the scope and administrability of the majority’s tailored-protection approach (especially Kagan/Gorsuch/Barrett, possibly Sotomayor).
